item.title: Hossain Zillur Rahman: Key to change lies in the hands of citizens
item.description:
A public lecture titled ‘What Drives Change: Today’s Questions’ was held on Thursday, July 30, at the 'Manzur Elahi' Auditorium of East West University.
Eminent economist and chairman of Brac Hossain Zillur Rahman delivered the keynote address.
In his speech, Rahman outlined six drivers of change: narrative, institution, norms, initiatives, power, and interest groups.
He highlighted how both the positive and negative aspects of these drivers impact the nation's economy.
Rahman emphasized that Bangladesh must move away from a cheap-labor-dependent economy that relies primarily on garments and remittances.
He noted that the country has struggled to embody democratic principles in state practices and has been unable to fully capitalize on its demographic dividend, leaving the economy stagnant.
To achieve positive change, he urged a focus on several key areas, including reforming the concept of the state to view it as a service to the people rather than as an entity above them.
He also called for addressing the lack of professionalism among local professionals, improving the quality of education with forward-looking foresight, and shifting social norms toward greater cleanliness and transparency.
Drawing historical parallels to 1947, 1971, and 2024, Dr. Rahman remarked that the persistent aspiration for change among the citizens of Bangladesh is the nation's greatest strength. In times of national crisis, citizen-led innovation and grassroots initiatives have consistently paved the path toward solutions.
Therefore, he concluded, the ultimate key to change lies in the hands of the citizens.
Presiding over the event, Prof Mohammed Farashuddin, chairperson of the board of trustees of East West University, highlighted that the benefits of national development are failing to reach the vulnerable and voiceless segments of society.
He called for special attention to healthcare and education for underprivileged populations and urged action to address the growing deficit of social equity.
Earlier, Prof Shams Rahman, vice chancellor of East West University, delivered the welcome address.
Members of the board of trustees, faculty members, students, officers, and staff of the university were present at the event.

item.title: Directorate of Posts gets Tk18.5cr revenue share from Nagad for FY26
item.description:
Mobile financial service (MFS) provider Nagad has handed over Tk18.56 crore to the Directorate of Posts as its revenue share for FY26, marking a 34% year-on-year increase.
The revenue share grew by over Tk5 crore compared to the figure in the previous fiscal year.
Bangladesh Bank-appointed Administrator for Nagad, Md Motasem Billah, handed over the cheque to Minister for Posts, Telecommunications and Information Technology Fakir Mahbub Anam, MP, at a ceremony at Daak Bhaban in the capital’s Agargaon Wednesday.
Posts and Telecommunications Secretary Bilquis Jahan Rimi, Director General of the Directorate of Posts Kazi Asadul Islam and senior officials from both organisations were present.
Minister for Posts, Telecommunications and Information Technology Fakir Mahbub Anam said: “Without Nagad, there will be a monopoly in the market, and we will not allow that to happen. Nagad must maintain a competitive market and become even more profitable.”
Calling on journalists present at the event not to heed any rumours regarding Nagad, the minister said there is no alternative to digital transactions for the development of people in remote areas, students, and general people.
​“People know Nagad is a state-backed institution. Therefore, we must move forward with Nagad through essential activities and services,” he added.
Posts and Telecommunications Secretary Bilkis Jahan Rimi said: “Today is a day of joy for us. The government has earned a substantial amount of revenue through Nagad. We will work on exploring further avenues for the Directorate of Posts to collaborate with Nagad.”
Director General of the Directorate of Posts Kazi Asadul Islam said: “We often hear that state-owned entities cannot turn a profit, but we have disproven that narrative through Nagad and demonstrated that government services can indeed be profitable.”
​Highlighting the operator’s financial contribution since its inception, the director general noted that Nagad has so far paid Tk946 crore in taxes to the government alongside Tk47 crore in revenue shares to the postal department.
​“In total, the government has received nearly Tk1,000 crore since Nagad’s inception, which is a significant achievement. Building on the trust and goodwill of marginalised people, we aim to move further forward in the days ahead,” he added.
Nagad Administrator Md Motasem Billah said Nagad has made an outstanding contribution to bringing marginalised people across the country under financial inclusion through technology.
“Besides driving innovations, Nagad plays the paramount role in safeguarding consumer interests by enhancing market competition. At the same time, the operator continues to play a vital role in generating revenue for the government every year,” he added.
Currently, the company records a daily average transaction volume exceeding Tk1,500 crore.
As per the partnership agreement, Nagad Limited bears all capital and operational expenditures, including technological infrastructure, requiring no financial investment from the postal department.
Following the deduction of specific allowable operational expenses from total revenue, the Directorate of Posts receives 51% of the net proceeds, while Nagad Limited retains the remaining 49%.
Before this latest payment, Nagad Limited had disbursed nearly Tk28.5 crore in cumulative revenue shares to the Postal Department since its inception.
With the addition of the disbursement for the recently concluded FY26, Nagad’s total revenue contribution to the Directorate of Posts stands at Tk47 crore.
Earlier in March 2026, Nagad handed over Tk13.82 crore for the 18 months spanning January 2024 to June 2025.
Previous disbursements included Tk5.51 crore in 2024 and Tk4.50 crore in 2022. Over the preceding years, Nagad provided Tk4.5 crore in revenue share to the postal department.
Beyond this, the MFS operator paid Tk313 crore to the exchequer in VAT and other taxes during the first 11 months of the current fiscal year.
In FY26, Nagad processed transactions totalling Tk427,000 crore – a 25.5% year-on-year growth from Tk340,000 crore in the preceding year.
Alongside the steady surge in transaction volume and count, the operator’s user base expanded substantially, with active customers surpassing 30 million as of June, including over 22.5 million app users.

'Govt takes hardline stance against human trafficking, online scams'
item.description:
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed on Thursday said the government has adopted a "zero tolerance" policy against human trafficking and technology-enabled transnational scam networks.
"Protecting citizens from trafficking and cyber-enabled exploitation remains a top priority," he said.
The minister made the remarks while speaking as the chief guest at a high-level national dialogue titled "Trapped behind the Scam: Ending Human Trafficking for Forced Criminality" at Pan Pacific Sonargaon Hotel in the capital, marking the World Day Against Trafficking in Persons 2026.
He said trafficking syndicates are increasingly using fake online recruitment platforms and social media to lure job seekers, particularly young people, with false promises of overseas employment.
Many victims are later confined in cyber scam centres abroad, where they are subjected to torture, intimidation and forced criminal activities, Salahuddin said.
He said conventional law enforcement alone is no longer sufficient to tackle the evolving threat and called for stronger collaboration among technology companies, financial institutions, the private sector and civil society.
Highlighting government initiatives, the minister said Bangladesh has enacted the Human Trafficking and Migrant Smuggling (Prevention and Suppression) Act, 2026, aligned with the UN Convention against Transnational Organized Crime (UNTOC) and its protocols.
The law brings online scam-related trafficking, technology-enabled deception and forced criminality under stricter legal penalties, he said.
Salahuddin also said the government is updating the Human Trafficking Prevention and Suppression Rules, 2017, while finalising the National Action Plan (2026-2030) focusing on prevention, protection, prosecution and partnership.
To strengthen victim support, he said the government is enhancing the National Referral Mechanism (NRM) to ensure timely rescue and provide legal, medical, psychological and rehabilitation services.
A digital trafficking information management platform is also being developed to improve case tracking and evidence-based policymaking, he added.
He urged the media and civil society to raise awareness among youths, women and prospective migrant workers about safe migration and the risks posed by fraudulent recruitment networks.
The dialogue, chaired by Senior Secretary of the Home Ministry Manzur Morshed Chowdhury, was attended by senior government officials, diplomats, law enforcement representatives and international partners, including the European Union, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) and the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC).
Special guests included Secretary of the Law and Justice Division Liaquet Ali Molla, Inspector General of Police (IGP) Md. Ali Hossain Fakir, Charg‚ d'Affaires of the European Union Baiba Zarina, and Dr. Laura Tomm-Bonde, IOM's new Chief of Mission in Bangladesh and Coordinator of the UN Migration Network.
Among those present were Director General of the Bangladesh Coast Guard Rear Admiral Md Ziaul Hoque and Additional Director General of Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) Brigadier General Md Sohrab Hossain Bhuiyan.
The welcome address was delivered by Additional Secretary of the Ministry of Home Affairs Dr. Ziauddin Ahmed, while Shah Mohammad Naheeaan, Head of the UNODC Programme Office in Bangladesh, presented this year's World Day Against Trafficking in Persons theme in detail.
A panel discussion on trafficking for forced criminality, deceptive recruitment and online exploitation was also held as part of the programme.

Shapla Chattar case: Latif Siddiqui sent to jail
item.description:
The International Crimes Tribunal has ordered former minister Abdul Latif Siddiqui to be shown arrested and sent to jail in a crimes against humanity case over the massacre surrounding the Hefazat-e-Islam rally at Shapla Chattar in Motijheel, Dhaka, on May 5, 2013.
The three-member International Crimes Tribunal, led by Justice Nazrul Islam Chowdhury, passed the order on Thursday after hearing a prosecution petition.
Abdul Latif Siddiqui was produced before the International Crimes Tribunal at 1pm on Thursday.
According to the prosecution, an arrest warrant had already been issued against Latif Siddiqui in the case filed over the Shapla Chattar incident. To execute the warrant, the Detective Branch (DB) of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) arrested him from his residence in Gulshan on Wednesday evening.
On July 27, after taking cognizance of the formal charges submitted by the prosecution, Tribunal-2 issued arrest warrants against 31 people, including ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina, and ordered 10 others to appear before the tribunal. The tribunal also set August 16 for the next hearing in the case.
Eight people are currently in custody in the case. They are former minister Dr Dipu Moni, former state minister for home affairs Shamsul Haque Tuku, Major General (retd) Ziaul Ahsan, former inspector general of police (IGP) AKM Shahidul Haque, Shahriar Kabir, president of the advisory council of Ekattorer Ghatak Dalal Nirmul Committee, former deputy inspector general (DIG) Abdul Jalil Mondal, journalist Farzana Rupa, and Mozammel Babu.
Hasanul Haq Inu is also in jail after being convicted in another case. Abdur Razzaq has also been arrested in the same case. The remaining accused are absconding.
The formal charges in the case contain two allegations of crimes against humanity. The first allegation concerns the killing of 32 people at Shapla Chattar on May 5, 2013.
The second allegation concerns the killing of 20 people, including Sadek Mia, in Narayanganj’s Siddhirganj on May 6, as well as deaths reported in different parts of the country.
The charges also include allegations that several people, including Rashedul Islam and Abu Yusuf, were shot with the intention of killing them and suffered serious injuries as a result of the attacks and torture.
The prosecution said these acts constitute crimes against humanity, including genocide, murder, attempted murder, torture, and persecution based on political and religious identity.

Extreme heat threatens jobs, economic growth in South Asia
item.description:
Extreme heat is costing South Asia nearly the equivalent of 31 million full-time jobs every year and is on track to reduce the region's economy by nearly 7% by 2050, according to a new World Bank report released on Wednesday.
As South Asia prepares to add 280 million working-age people by 2050, rising temperatures are one of the greatest threats to jobs, productivity, and long-term economic growth in the region.
"A Livable Future: Protecting Jobs and Growth from Extreme Heat in South Asia's Cities" finds that by 2070, around 520 million people across South Asia could experience at least one month of dangerous heat each year, four times as many as today. Extreme heat is already reducing labour productivity, disrupting businesses, and jeopardizing the competitiveness of South Asia's cities. It is also putting growing pressure on health systems and critical infrastructure, while hitting low-income households, informal workers, women, the elderly, and children the hardest.
"South Asia's cities are central to the region's future, but rising temperatures are putting jobs, livelihoods, and economic growth at risk," said Johannes Zutt, World Bank Vice President for South Asia.
"Building heat- resilient cities is not only about protecting people from rising temperatures. It is about safeguarding jobs, boosting productivity, attracting investment, and ensuring cities continue to drive economic growth. By acting now, countries can build more resilient, competitive, and livable cities that create opportunities for future generations."
The report examines extreme heat through the lens of jobs, productivity, and economic growth. It shows how rising temperatures affect workers, businesses, infrastructure, public services, and urban economies. The report argues that heat should no longer be treated as a seasonal emergency. Instead, it should become a core development priority that is integrated into urban planning, infrastructure investment, public policy, and private sector development.
The report provides policymakers with a practical roadmap that can be implemented through existing institutions and financing mechanisms. It recommends investing in heat resilient infrastructure, strengthening Heat Action Plans, protecting vulnerable workers, expanding sustainable cooling, improving early warning systems, and mobilizing public and private investment to build more resilient cities.
This report was prepared with support from the Resilient Asia Program (RAP), funded by the UK Government’s Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO) through its flagship Climate Action for a Resilient Asia (CARA) program. The World Bank’s Global Facility for Disaster Reduction and Recovery (GFDRR) and the City Resilience Program (CRP) also supported the preparation of the report.
“Across South Asia, extreme heat is destroying livelihoods, impacting public health, depressing productivity, and pushing the most vulnerable further into poverty,” said John Warburton, Climate Resilience Lead for Asia Pacific at UK’s Foreign Commonwealth and Development Office. “This is a development crisis that calls for sustained action across sectors. That is why the UK government, through our flagship Climate Action for a Resilient Asia programme, is committed to working with the World Bank and other partners to build knowledge, inform policies, and unlock the investment needs in the region to adapt to a warming planet.”
Many of the solutions already exist. Cities across South Asia are showing how Heat Action Plans, resilient infrastructure, urban greening, early warning systems, and efficient cooling can save lives, protect workers, and reduce economic losses. Scaling these approaches will require stronger institutions, better coordination, and greater public and private investment.
As South Asia continues to urbanize, the choices governments make today will determine whether cities remain engines of jobs, innovation and growth, or become increasingly constrained by rising temperatures. Investing in heat resilience is essential to protect people, strengthen economies, and secure the region's long-term prosperity.
*The South Asia Region includes Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, and Sri Lanka.

item.title: Tripura CM sends pineapples to PM Tarique reciprocating mango gift
item.description:
Tripura Chief Minister Dr Manik Saha on Wednesday sent 600 Queen variety pineapples to Prime Minister Tarique Rahman as a goodwill gesture, reciprocating a recent gift of mangoes from the Bangladesh government.
The consignment arrived through the Akhaura Land Port in Brahmanbaria around 1pm.
Packed in 100 cartons, the pineapples were transported by a pickup from the northeastern Indian state of Tripura.
Officials from the Assistant High Commission of India in Chittagong received the consignment before handing it over to representatives of the Indian High Commission in Dhaka for onward delivery.
The pineapples were later transported to the capital by pickup.
Apurba Roy, secretary of Tripura's Agriculture Department, who was present at the port, said the gift was sent in response to the mangoes recently presented by the Bangladesh government.
"The Bangladesh government gifted us mangoes. On behalf of our state, we are sending pineapples as a gift," he said.

item.title: Alleged top criminal David Emon arrested in Jessore
item.description:
Detective Branch (DB) police on Wednesday arrested alleged top criminal Mobarak Hossain Emon, also known as David Emon, in Jessore.
Jessore Additional Superintendent of Police (Crime) Mirajul Islam confirmed the arrest to Dhaka Tribune at around 2pm.
"DB police arrested David Emon from a vehicle in the Jhumjhumpur area on the Jessore-Narail Highway. He is now in the custody of Jessore police. Details will be provided later," he said.
According to police, Emon and Mohammad Raihan allegedly took over leadership of a criminal syndicate in Chittagong after the arrest of Chhoto Sajjad, an alleged associate of fugitive criminal Sajjad Ali Khan. Investigators alleged that Chhoto Sajjad had previously carried out criminal activities on behalf of Boro Sajjad.
Police said followers of Sajjad Ali Khan have been behind most recent extortion demands and attacks in Chittagong city and the upazilas of Raozan, Hathazari and Fatikchhari. Law enforcement agencies had been searching for both Emon and Raihan before Wednesday's arrest.
One of the cases linked to Emon is an alleged extortion attempt targeting Digital Dot Net (DDN), a Chittagong-based business.
According to police, DDN owner Adil Bin Mamun received a call from a foreign number on July 11 from a person identifying himself as David Emon, who allegedly demanded Tk20 million in extortion and threatened further attacks if the money was not paid.
Police said that two days later, at around 12:30pm on July 13, about 30 to 35 armed men attacked the DDN office on the Chandanpura-Bakalia Access Road under Chawkbazar Police Station.
The assailants allegedly vandalized the office, looted Tk3.5 million kept there for salary payments and warned the company against continuing its operations. CCTV footage of the attack later circulated on social media.
Police said the attacked office is adjacent to the residence of Smart Group Director Mujibur Rahman, where gunfire was reported on February 28 while the house was under police protection. Investigators alleged that followers of fugitive criminal Sajjad Ali Khan carried out the attack after failing to extort money from the businessman.
The same residence also came under gunfire on January 2, when bullets struck its windows and doors. Police protection remained in place following the incident.
Earlier, Chittagong police arrested two alleged associates of Emon from the Wazedia area on the Oxygen-Kuaish Road, recovering a foreign-made pistol and four rounds of ammunition.
The suspects, identified as Md Asif, 25, and Saidul Islam, alias Arif, 24, were arrested on Sunday night. Police said Asif was a fugitive accused in a criminal case.

item.title: Law minister: Govt taken effective initiatives to reduce civil case backlog
item.description:
Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs Minister Md Asaduzzaman on Wednesday said the present government has taken effective initiatives to reduce longstanding civil case backlog.
"Various reform initiatives are being implemented to make the judicial process faster, more efficient and more people-friendly. Backlog of cases could be reduced and the efficiency of the judicial process enhanced through the exchange of domestic and international experiences and mutual cooperation," he said.
The minister made the remarks at a seminar titled "Addressing Delays in the Disposal of Civil Cases: Shared Experiences of Bangladesh and Japan" at Judicial Administration Training Institute (JATI). Law and Justice Division and Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) jointly organized the seminar, an official release said on Wednesday.
Md Asaduzzaman said that many civil cases in Bangladesh are still pending despite having remained unresolved for many years. The prolonged pendency of these cases has increased the sufferings of litigants and placed an additional burden on the judicial system, he added.
"To address this situation, the government is implementing various reform initiatives, including modernizing the judiciary, expanding Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR), introducing technology-driven judicial services, and making the judicial process simpler and more efficient," he further said.
The law minister also said the experiences and cooperation of the Japanese Ministry of Justice and international partners, including the JICA, would play a significant role in strengthening Bangladesh's judicial system.
"Such joint initiatives would create new opportunities for the exchange of knowledge and experiences between the two countries, which would make a positive contribution to enhancing the efficiency of the judicial process," he added.
Speaking as the special guest, Deputy Director-General of the International Cooperation Department of Japan's Ministry of Justice, Kazunori Nose, assured that Japan would continue its cooperation in strengthening and enhancing the capacity of Bangladesh's judicial system.
The keynote papers were presented by Senior Assistant Secretary of the Law and Justice Division Syed Md Shafayet and Professor Wakazono Rei of Japan's Ministry of Justice. Project Director of the relevant project and Additional Secretary of the Law and Justice Division Md Khadem Ul Kayes chaired the seminar.

item.title: PM meets Tahsin, who lost sister in Milestone tragedy
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Wednesday met Tahsin Abdullah, a schoolboy whose heartwarming smile at the closing ceremony of the Notun Kuri Sports 2025-26 touched millions, a year after the boy lost his elder sister in the Milestone School fighter jet crash.
Learning the heartbreaking story behind the widely shared photograph of the smiling boy on social media, the prime minister met Tahsin and his father Nazmul Haque at the prime minister's office at Bangladesh Secretariat on Wednesday, said PM’s Assistant Press Secretary Gazi Shahriar Pamir.
A photograph of Tahsin during the closing ceremony of the “Notun Kuri Sports 2025-26” at Bangladesh Army Stadium in the capital on July 27 went viral on social media, showing Tahsin in his school uniform stretching out both hands towards the prime minister with an expression of pure joy. But behind that heartwarming smile was a story of deep personal grief.
In July 2025, Tahsin lost his elder sister Tasnia in the tragic fighter jet crash at Milestone School in Uttara. Although both siblings studied at the same school, they were in separate buildings on that fateful day. Tahsin was then a sixth-grade student, while Tasnia was an eighth-grader. The fighter jet crashed into the building where Tasnia was attending classes.
Hearing the deafening explosion, young Tahsin rushed to find his elder sister. After hearing that saline and water were needed, he stood waiting with bottles of saline and water in his small hands for his sister. But that wait never ended.
According to his family, the tragedy changed Tahsin completely. During a healing session after the incident, he wrote: “I am in great pain. I have lost my beloved sister. She died. I miss her so, so much. She was my best friend.”
Since losing his sister, Tahsin's once cheerful and lively smile was rarely seen. But on July 27 was a different day. At the Bangladesh Army Stadium, as Prime Minister Tarique Rahman was moving around the field during the closing ceremony, Tahsin became overwhelmed with joy when the prime minister came near him.
His innocent smile and excitement were captured on camera, and the photograph later spread widely on social media, with many people connecting emotionally with the boy’s happiness.
Later, the prime minister came to know that behind the smiling face in the photograph was a heartbreaking family history. After learning the details, he directed his Additional Press Secretary Atikur Rahman Rumon to take steps to inquire about Tahsin and his family.
As Tahsin arrived at prime minister’s office, the prime minister enquired about Tahsin's studies and ambitions. Tahsin said he wanted to become a successful businessman and do something that would benefit people and attract them.
The prime minister appreciated his dream and advised the young boy to concentrate on his studies, play sports regularly and work with sincerity and dedication to achieve his goals, Pamir said.
During the conversation, Tahsin said football was his favorite sports. The prime minister gifted him a basketball bearing his autograph and a drone set.
After the meeting, an excited Tahsin said he was very happy to meet the prime minister again. He said he never imagined he would get such an opportunity and described the entire experience as a complete surprise. He said he was eagerly waiting to go to school and share the story of meeting the prime minister with his friends.
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman also expressed deep sympathy and condolence to Tahsin’s father over the tragic loss of his daughter in the Milestone fighter jet crash.
PM’s Additional Press Secretary Atikur Rahman Rumon, Private Secretary-2 Md Mehedul Islam, Assistant Private Secretary-2 Abdur Rahman Sani, Associate Professor (Orthopedics) Dr Shah Muhammad Aman Ullah, Deputy Press Secretary Jahidul Islam Rony and Amra BNP Poribar Member Secretary Moksedul Momin Mithun were present.

item.description:
Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami on Wednesday demanded that the Election Commission withdraw its proposed provision barring MPO-listed teachers from contesting local government elections and cancel the contractual appointment of an additional secretary over “political affiliation”.
A six-member Jamaat delegation, led by its Secretary General Mia Golam Parwar, sat in a meeting with Chief Election Commissioner AMM Nasir Uddin at the Nirbachan Bhaban in Dhaka's Agargaon and submitted a letter to the CEC.
Election Commissioners Abdur Rahmanel Masud and Tahmida Ahmad, along with EC Senior Secretary Akhtar Ahmed, were also present at the meeting in the morning.
According to a letter submitted to the CEC, Jamaat also demanded consideration of its previous opinions regarding the local government election code of conduct, which were placed before the Election Commission on June 30 last.
In the letter, Jamaat said the EC has sent a proposal to the Ministry of Local Government declaring MPO-affiliated teachers ineligible to contest in local government elections.
If the proposed provision is implemented, several lakhs of teachers and employees of more than 30,000 MPO-affiliated educational institutions in the country will be deprived of the opportunity to participate in local government elections, which is inconsistent with the principles of equality and non-discrimination enshrined in Articles 27 and 28 of the Constitution, it added.
“So, we believe that the proposed provision needs to be reconsidered and withdrawn or amended so that the constitutional right of eligible citizens to political participation remains intact,” it said.
Jamaat also demanded the immediate cancellation of the recent contractual appointment of 67-year-old Md Shamsul Alam as an additional secretary to the EC Secretariat, alleging that he had links with a political party.
The party claimed that media reports regarding his alleged political affiliation have raised questions among people about the neutrality of the Election Commission.
The Jamaat delegation also included Assistant Secretaries General Dr AHM Hamidur Rahman Azad, Ahsanul Mahboob Zubair and Moazzem Hossain Helal, members of its central working committee Jasim Uddin Sarkar and Shishir Mohammad Monir.

item.title: Fire on Parliament premises under control; probe committee ordered
item.description:
A fire that broke out at the office of the Public Works Department outside the main Parliament complex on Tuesday afternoon has been brought under control.
The fire started at around 3:15pm at the office of the Executive Engineer of Public Works Department-1 of the complex, said a press release issued by the Parliament Secretariat.
On receiving the news, members of the Fire Service and Civil Defence rushed to the spot and brought the fire under control within a short time.
No casualty was reported in the incident, and the cause of the fire could not be ascertained.
Acting Speaker Barrister Kayser Kamal and the secretary of the Parliament Secretariat visited the spot soon after being informed of the incident.
The acting speaker directed the formation of an investigation committee to determine the actual cause of the fire, assess the extent of damage and make recommendations for preventing such incidents in the future.
Details about the cause of the fire and other related matters will be made public after receiving the investigation committee's report, said the release signed by Director (Public Relations) of Parliament Secretariat Monir Hossain.

item.title: Over 53.94% of Khulna primary schools running without head teachers
item.description:
More than half of the government primary schools in Khulna Division are operating without head teachers, creating challenges for academic management and administrative activities.
Of the division’s 8,165 government primary schools, 4,405 have vacant head teacher posts, meaning 53.94% of schools do not have permanent heads, according to the Primary Education Directorate.
Among these schools, 1,348 are currently being managed by assistant teachers serving as acting head teachers.
Md Shariful Islam, deputy director of primary education in Khulna Division, said the shortage exists across all 10 districts of the division.
“Of the total schools, 4,405 have vacant head teacher posts,” he said.
The number of schools without head teachers is 605 in Khulna, 672 in Bagerhat, 468 in Satkhira, 691 in Jashore, 523 in Jhenaidah, 271 in Magura, 415 in Kushtia, 287 in Chuadanga, 320 in Narail and 153 in Meherpur.
Assistant teachers are performing acting head teacher duties in 1,348 schools, including 301 in Jessore, 255 in Satkhira, 188 in Bagerhat and 131 in Khulna.
Khulna District Primary Education Officer Sheikh Ahidul Alam said 605 out of 1,159 government primary schools in the district are without head teachers.
The highest number of vacancies is in Dumuria, where 113 schools have no head teacher, followed by Koyra with 85 schools and Paikgachha with 73 schools.
Other affected areas include Khulna Sadar with 56 schools, Dakop 55, Batiaghata 52, Rupsha 37, Phultala 39, Terokhada 62 and Dighalia 33.
Sheikh Ahidul Alam said documents for promoting eligible assistant teachers to head teacher positions have already been sent to the Directorate of Primary Education.
“Once the recruitment and promotion process is completed through the Bangladesh Public Service Commission and the Directorate, the vacant posts can gradually be filled,” he said.
He added that around 300 schools in Khulna were assigned acting head teachers in 2018, but the number has declined due to retirement and death of teachers.
Koyra upazila is among the worst affected areas, with 85 out of 142 government primary schools operating without head teachers.
According to the upazila primary education office, these schools have 22,806 students.
Officials said no head teacher has been appointed to any primary school in Koyra since 2013.
Several schools, including Gobra Ghatakhali Government Primary School, Uttar Madinabad Government Primary School, Swarnakali Government Primary School and Srirampur Government Primary School, are currently without permanent heads.
The upazila also has 42 vacant assistant teacher posts.
Habibur Rahman, a resident of Gobra village whose son studies at Gobra Ghatakhali Government Primary School, said the absence of a head teacher has affected academic activities.
“Teaching has been disrupted. A permanent head teacher should be appointed soon to improve the learning environment,” he said.
Acting head teachers said managing both classroom teaching and administrative responsibilities has become increasingly difficult.
They said preparing official reports, maintaining records, handling accounts and implementing government instructions often leave them with less time for teaching.
Md Billal Hossain, acting head teacher of Gobra Ghatakhali Government Primary School, has been performing the additional responsibility since 2023.
The school has 157 students and five assistant teachers, including him.
“Appointing a permanent head teacher would help improve the overall management of the school,” he said.
Officials said legal complications are also contributing to the prolonged vacancies.
Nurul Amin, acting head teacher of Swarnakali Government Primary School, said a case over the status and ranking of teachers from 10 schools that were brought under government management is still pending.
He said the unresolved case has created uncertainty over promotions and postings of teachers from those schools.
Students of Shyamnagar Government Primary School said some teachers cannot take regular classes as they are engaged in additional administrative duties.
The Koyra Upazila Primary Education Office is also facing manpower shortages.
Three of the five posts of assistant upazila education officers are vacant, while all four office assistant positions have remained unfilled for a long time.
Koyra Upazila Primary Education Officer Tapan Kumar Karmakar said acting responsibilities have been assigned to assistant teachers for 16 vacant head teacher posts.
He said steps have been taken to fill some positions, but legal complications have delayed the process.

item.title: It turns people into animals: Bangladesh’s growing yaba addiction crisis
item.description:
“Metalfreak” once spent hours caring for his pet bird every day, stroking her, cleaning her cage and letting her fly freely. Now, he says, he cannot even bring himself to do that. “Who cares?” he says, lying on his bed in his cluttered Dhaka bedroom.
The man in his forties, who asked to go by his chosen pseudonym, has an increasingly debilitating addiction to yaba, a drug mixing methamphetamine and caffeine, which is destroying lives in Bangladesh.
Yaba, which means “crazy medicine” in Thai, is thought to be used by millions of Bangladeshis, with numbers continuing to rise.
To consume it, Metalfreak puts a pill on tinfoil and heats it from below, before inhaling the fumes. The impact of each of the orange pills lasts four to five hours, he says. He stays awake for three days at a time before crashing and sleeping for 12 hours or more.
In June, Bangladeshi home minister Salahuddin Ahmed said nearly 5 per cent of the country’s population of roughly 175 million people have a drug addiction, and “the emergence of new synthetic and semi-synthetic drugs” was “further intensifying the problem,” according to local media. This month Bangladesh’s parliament approved a Bill retaining the death penalty for some drugs-related offences.
Yaba is considered a class-A banned substance in Bangladesh. In 2018, under ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina, there was a crackdown by authorities, with more than 200 people killed in a few months in behaviour reminiscent of Filipino president Rodrigo Duterte’s brutal “war on drugs”.
The killings have led to concerned pronouncements by the EU and the UN high commissioner for human rights. Amnesty International has said 466 people were killed in 2018, saying what was presented as an anti-drugs campaign “spread terror in some of the country’s poorest neighbourhoods, where people fear the slightest suspicion of being involved in drug abuse may lead to their loved ones being subjected to another alleged extrajudicial execution”. Tens of thousands more were arrested, reports the Irish Times.
Yet usage continues to rise, local experts say. “If we want to reduce substance use, we have to improve mental health services,” says Dr Md Arifuzzaman, a registrar at the National Institute of Mental Health, who also works at Niramoy rehabilitation centre in Dhaka. “Life is waiting where recovery begins” is written on the wall behind its reception.
There are about 350 psychiatrists in the whole country, he says. In the National Institute, psychiatrists might see 20 patients in one hour, “but we have no other option”. He says there is a similar lack of qualified psychologists in Bangladesh. He wants the government to integrate mental health into primary healthcare. Bangladesh’s last national mental health survey, carried out in 2018-2019, found that about 90 per cent of people who need mental healthcare do not seek treatment. Arifuzzaman says stigma around mental health is “prevailing all over the world, in our country as well,” but in the past few years awareness has increased a “magnificent amount”.
Yaba addiction is “very common”, though many users use other drugs too, which could include buprenorphine injections, heroin, and omorphone tablets, he says. Almost every substance is increasing in use, with yaba usage “significantly increasing.”
He says some users remain “functional”, while others have “vulnerabilities in the brain” that mean they will be more affected. Certain external events – such as crises related to flooding, fires and the Covid-19 pandemic can also trigger the situation.
Arifuzzaman says some users become dealers because they have no other way to support their habit. Some users were originally dealing with mental conditions, such as depression, anxiety disorders or psychosis, and were seeking relief when they turned to drugs.
The availability of substances clearly plays a role in which drugs are commonly taken, Arifuzzaman says. Yaba was traditionally used in parts of Asia by occupational workers such as truck drivers, before shifting into “youth culture” in the late 1990s, according to the UN Office on Drugs and Crime. In 2007, 1.2 million tablets were confiscated in Bangladesh, the body said.
The area where Thailand, Myanmar and Laos meet, known as the Golden Triangle, is believed to be one of the world’s most active areas for the production of synthetic drugs. The UN Office on Drugs and Crime says a record 236 tonnes of methamphetamine (commonly known as meth) were seized in east and southeast Asia in 2024, a 24 per cent increase on 2023, with much more likely going on sale. Myanmar is believed to be the main producer of the yaba in Bangladesh.
“Everyone has the same sob story,” says Metalfreak. He says Bangladeshis who become addicted to yaba usually start with cigarettes, then weed, then cough syrup. As a young man, he was familiar with “downers” such as cannabis. The first time he took yaba he was expecting it would be good to “hang, chill” but it “put my mind through the roof ... This thing makes people animal.”
Yaba used to be more expensive. Now there are two categories of the drug available: cheap and expensive. The cheaper versions “totally f**k” your mouth and teeth, he says, while “you can see in [a user’s] eyes they’re crazy.” Metalfreak says he has lost friends to these pills – taking it consistently can lead to a stroke, he says. Others lose teeth or start “twitching”.
In the past few years, it has become harder to get opium or heroin, Metalfreak says. Yaba “totally kicked out all other drugs”. In Dhaka it is easy to spot young people selling packets of the pills on the street. In an area called Mohammadpur, young boys hold up sachets of the pills while rickshaw drivers reach to take them.
Bangladesh has experienced political instability in recent years. As many as 1,400 people are thought to have been killed during 2024 protests that led to Hasina’s ousting, before a 2026 election led to a victory for the Bangladesh Nationalist Party, led by Tarique Rahman. Classified as a lower-middle-income country by the World Bank, the south Asian country has also been assessed as particularly vulnerable to climate change by various global rankings. Many young people worry about their future.
All of this upheaval has personal implications. Metalfreak’s father, who recently died, was lauded as a freedom fighter, he says, but more recently friends dismiss him as a “fraud”. Metalfreak ran a business, but the premises burnt down in a type of fire that seems surprisingly common in Bangladesh – he thinks it was done on purpose, though others say it could have been an electrical fault or another type of accident.
When he engages with the world now, it is through Instagram, where he watches endless videos about Gaza. Brown people and Muslims in particular are treated as worthless globally, he says, adding that he has despaired at the western media and the US.
Metalfreak says yaba gives people “false confidence”, with many believing “weird conspiracy theories”. His conversation meanders, veering into thoughts on Kim Jong-un, Uyghurs in China, Kneecap, Venezuela, Aung San Suu Kyi and Vladimir Putin.
Metalfreak says the economic situation influences everything in Bangladesh – terrorism, crime and addiction. He thinks better-off people are the ones with time to develop addictions. “I’m privileged ... I have a room. I can lie down. I don’t have to think tomorrow: about who’s going feed me, feed my family.”
He worries about the impact of the drugs: how yaba users “will never last two years” because they don’t sleep. “It’s a slow poisoning, it’s a meticulous plan.”

item.description:
Social Welfare Minister Dr AZM Zahid Hossain on Tuesday said if advanced treatment for hepatitis B can be ensured within the country, it will reduce patients' tendency to travel abroad for treatment as well as cut medical costs.

This year's theme for the day is "Elimination for Everyone, Everywhere, Right Now."
Minister Zahid said a significant section of Bangladesh's population is suffering from fatty liver disease without being aware of it.
He said the number of fatty liver patients in the country is rising day by day due to excessive carbohydrate intake, and called upon all concerned to raise public awareness on the issue.
Referring to the appointment of Professor Simon Taylor-Robinson, emeritus professor of Hepatology at Imperial College London, to the Department of Hepatology at BMU, the minister said involving foreign and regional experts to evaluate students against international and regional standards would play an important role in improving the quality of medical education.
He urged other medical colleges to take similar timely initiatives.
At one point during the event, members of the Gastroenterology Society of Bangladesh demanded that hepatitis B screening be made mandatory for all pregnant women.

item.title: ULAB hosts workshop, cultural performance on Manipuri heritage

The event was held on Tuesday under the chairmanship of Professor Shahnaj Husne Jahan, head of the Department of General Education. Students, faculty members from different departments and invited guests attended the programme.
The academic session was conducted by Manipuri researcher Sukanta Sinha, who spoke on the history, cultural heritage, social life, festivals, music, dance traditions and artistic legacy of the Manipuri community. The session concluded with an interactive question-and-answer segment.
A highlight of the event was a live Pung (Manipuri drum) performance and a classical Manipuri dance recital by Arnab Sharma, adjunct faculty member of the Department of Dance at the University of Dhaka. His performance showcased the aesthetics, rhythm, spirituality and expressive traditions of Manipuri performing arts.
According to the organizers, the combination of academic discussion and live cultural performances provided students with an experiential learning opportunity while fostering a greater appreciation of Bangladesh’s cultural diversity and intangible cultural heritage.
ULAB and MAATRA Gobeshona Songstha said the initiative reflects their shared commitment to promoting indigenous knowledge, preserving cultural heritage, encouraging intercultural dialogue and enriching students’ learning through academic and cultural engagement.

item.title: BSTI advises against swallowing toothpaste amid microplastics debate
item.description:
The Bangladesh Standards and Testing Institution (BSTI) has urged the public not to panic over a recent study that detected microplastics in several toothpaste brands sold in the country, advising consumers to maintain proper oral hygiene and avoid swallowing toothpaste.
In a press release issued on Tuesday, BSTI said no toothpaste brand or product should be declared unsafe or substandard before the findings are scientifically and legally verified.
The statement comes after the Environment and Social Development Organization (ESDO), a private research organisation, reported detecting microplastics in 26 of 34 toothpaste samples tested. BSTI said it is treating the findings with utmost importance because of their potential implications for public health and the environment.
According to BSTI, microplastics are plastic particles measuring 5 millimetres or less that are generally invisible to the bare eye. The World Health Organization (WHO said that microplastics are an emerging environmental and public health concern, although there is still no conclusive scientific evidence on their health risks. It stressed that further research is needed.
The press release also outlined international regulatory developments. It noted that the United States banned the intentional use of plastic microbeads in rinse-off cosmetic products, including toothpaste, under the Microbead-Free Waters Act in 2015. The European Union has given manufacturers until October 17, 2027, to phase out the use of intentionally added microplastics in such products.
However, BSTI said neither South Asian countries, including India, Pakistan and Sri Lanka, nor international standards organisations have established a maximum permissible limit or a standard testing method for microplastics in toothpaste.
The agency said toothpaste manufacturers and importers in Bangladesh are required to obtain licences under BDS 1216:2012 Specification for Toothpaste before producing or marketing their products. Under government regulations, licences are issued only after products undergo chemical, microbiological and safety testing.
BSTI further said the country's approved list of 81 ingredients for toothpaste manufacturing does not include microplastics. It also evaluates manufacturers' quality control systems before granting licences, making the intentional use of microplastics unlikely.
The standards body stressed that the detection of plastic particles alone does not prove they were intentionally added by manufacturers or that they pose a risk to human health. Determining the particles' type, source, concentration and potential health risks requires further scientific analysis, it added.
As part of its review, BSTI has requested ESDO to provide the study's full report, testing methodology, raw data and other relevant documents. It is also collecting information from the manufacturers and importers concerned on raw materials, product ingredients and the use of synthetic polymers.

item.title: How to protect yourself from hepatitis
item.description:
Hepatitis B and C have emerged as major public health concerns in Bangladesh.
According to the World Health Organization (WHO), Bangladesh is among the 10 countries with the highest number of hepatitis C infections. However, timely vaccination, testing and treatment can prevent many cases and reduce complications.
Health experts say one of the biggest challenges is that people infected with viral hepatitis often show no symptoms for years. As a result, the disease is frequently diagnosed only after serious complications, such as liver cirrhosis or liver cancer, have developed.
WHO Representative to Bangladesh Dr Ahmed Jamsheed Mohamed said: “Hepatitis is preventable, treatable and, in the case of hepatitis C, curable. But many people develop severe complications because they do not receive timely testing and medical care.”
WHO recommends administering the first dose of the hepatitis B vaccine within 24 hours of birth, followed by all recommended doses, to provide the best protection.
Blood should always be screened for hepatitis B, hepatitis C and other infectious diseases before transfusion.
Always ensure that sterile syringes, needles and medical equipment are used for injections, dental procedures, tattoos and piercings. Reusing equipment significantly increases the risk of infection.
Avoid sharing razors, toothbrushes, nail clippers or any other items that may come into contact with blood.
Hepatitis B can spread through blood and bodily fluids. Practising safe sex helps reduce the risk of transmission.
People with a history of blood transfusions, a family history of hepatitis, healthcare workers and others at higher risk should undergo hepatitis B and C screening. Early diagnosis improves treatment outcomes.
Testing pregnant women for hepatitis B allows healthcare providers to take steps to reduce the risk of mother-to-child transmission.
Although hepatitis often causes no symptoms, seek medical advice if you experience jaundice, dark urine, persistent fatigue, loss of appetite or prolonged pain in the upper right side of the abdomen.
According to WHO, hepatitis B can be effectively managed with medication, while hepatitis C can be cured in most cases with modern antiviral drugs. Early treatment is crucial.
WHO says social stigma and misconceptions often discourage people from getting tested or treated. Raising awareness and supporting people living with hepatitis without discrimination are essential to controlling the disease.
Experts say the most effective tools against hepatitis are awareness, timely vaccination, regular screening of at-risk groups and prompt treatment. Expanding access to prevention and treatment services, along with strengthening the healthcare system and public awareness, could significantly reduce hepatitis-related deaths in Bangladesh.

item.title: Rampal cluster village struggles with multiple problems
item.description:
A cluster village established for families displaced by the Rampal Thermal Power Plant is facing severe waterlogging, inadequate public services and barriers to education, with residents blaming poor infrastructure for deteriorating living conditions and an increase in child marriages.
Located at Kaigaddaskathi behind the power plant, the village is home to around 800 families, although only 142 households have received government-built houses.
Residents say an earthen embankment constructed around the village has trapped rainwater and household wastewater because no drainage system was built, leaving the area submerged for nearly nine months each year.
The prolonged waterlogging has created unhygienic conditions, with overflowing toilets and stagnant water contributing to widespread skin diseases, including rashes and itching among children and adults.
"We have nowhere for the water to go," said Rafiza Begum. "When it rains, the toilets overflow and we are forced to walk through dirty water."
Residents said they had previously lived on khas land before it was acquired for the power plant. Each family was later allocated 1.75 decimals of land on a nearby river char for rehabilitation. Initially, all lived in makeshift shelters before some received permanent houses under government housing programmes.
Parents say access to education has become one of the settlement's biggest challenges.
Although a primary school is located nearby, there is no secondary school within six kilometres, forcing students either to travel to Borni or cross the river to Chalna.
For many families, particularly those with daughters, the journey is considered unsafe and too costly.
"As parents, we worry about our daughters travelling such long distances," said Asiya Begum. "Transport costs are high and crossing the river is risky. Many families end up arranging marriages instead."
Residents claim at least 15 child marriages have taken place in the settlement over the past two years, citing poverty, insecurity and limited educational opportunities as key factors.
Residents also say healthcare remains difficult to access despite living close to the power plant.
According to them, reaching the hospital associated with the project requires travelling 15 to 16 kilometres because of poor road connectivity and limited transport services. As a result, many rely on the health centre across the river in Chalna.
Ershad Ali said families who lost land to the project have received few long-term economic benefits.
"Our land was acquired, but local people have not found jobs at the power plant," he said. "We are also facing an acute shortage of safe drinking water."
In neighbouring Kapasdanga village, resident Ila Devi said there are three primary schools within three kilometres but no nearby secondary school.
She said it costs around Tk50 a day for one student to travel to school, an expense many low-income families cannot afford.
"I can only send my daughter to school twice a week," she said.
Riya Mondal said girls travelling to the secondary school in Chalna often have to wade through knee-deep saline water during high tide before boarding a ferry.
"They attend classes in wet clothes after crossing the river," she said. "Many parents do not want to take that risk."
Rampal Upazila Nirbahi Officer Tamanna Ferdousi said child marriage could not be justified under any circumstances.
"The area may not have been under adequate monitoring," she said. "Necessary steps will be taken through the Department of Women's Affairs to strengthen monitoring and prevent child marriage."
Responding to complaints of waterlogging, the UNO said no formal complaint had previously reached the administration but added that the matter would be investigated through the relevant project officials and necessary measures taken if required.

item.title: Pineapple farming takes root in Naogaon mango orchards
item.description:
Pineapple cultivation is gaining momentum in Naogaon’s Barind region as farmers are using vacant spaces between mango trees to grow the sweet fruit as an intercrop, creating new economic opportunities for the area.
The soil and climatic conditions of Porsha, Sapahar, and Patnitala upazilas are considered highly suitable for pineapple farming, with the region’s land consisting mainly of loamy and sandy-loamy soil. As pineapple cultivation requires relatively low investment while offering good returns, it is adding a new dimension to the rural economy.
Farmers are now cultivating MB-2 and Honey Queen varieties of pineapple in the unused spaces of mango orchards. It takes around 15 to 18 months from planting saplings to harvesting fruit. By producing two crops from the same land, farmers are improving land utilisation and increasing their income.
Due to favourable yields, pineapples grown in Naogaon are meeting local demand and are also being supplied to different parts of the country. Once established, pineapple plants can continue producing fruit for several years with minimal additional costs. The pineapples produced in the region are gaining popularity for their sweetness and distinctive taste.
Young agricultural entrepreneur Rayhan Siddiq of Porsha has become the first person in Naogaon to achieve commercial success through pineapple cultivation.
Rayhan said he planted 3,000 pineapple saplings collected from the Badalgachhi Horticulture Centre in 2024 during the rainy season. “After planting, I did not need to provide any irrigation. I only removed weeds and applied pesticides a few times. The pineapples have grown with very little expense,” he said.
He has already sold pineapples worth Tk 10,000 and expects to sell additional fruits worth around Tk 100,000. “The biggest advantage is that mangoes and pineapples can be cultivated on the same land. The cost is very low, and the fruits are extremely tasty,” he added.
Rayhan said he plans to expand pineapple cultivation on a larger scale. “We usually bring pineapples from Tangail and other districts to meet local demand. If pineapple farming expands in this mango-growing region, we will be able to fulfil the district’s demand with locally produced fruits,” he said.
Young agricultural entrepreneur Abdus Sobhan from Manda visited Rayhan’s farm after hearing that pineapple cultivation had started in Naogaon for the first time. “Rayhan Bhai offered me pineapple from his farm. It was very sweet. I have decided to start pineapple cultivation as well,” he said.
Another visitor, Tasnim, said she had never seen pineapple cultivation in Naogaon before. “I came after hearing about it and tasted the fruit. The flavour was amazing. I never imagined pineapples from this region could be so sweet,” she said.
Fruit trader Yasin Ali said they conduct fruit trading throughout the year. “Rayhan Bhai is the first person to cultivate pineapples commercially in this district. We came to buy his fruits. The production is good, and the market price is also encouraging,” he said.
Motahar Mia, a worker who has long been employed at Rayhan’s mango orchard, now also takes care of the pineapple plants. He believes Naogaon’s soil is highly suitable for pineapple cultivation.
Porsha Upazila Sub-Assistant Agriculture Officer Samirul Islam said Rayhan’s pineapple cultivation in a mango orchard is an excellent example of intercrop farming. “He is the first farmer in the district to commercially cultivate pineapples between mango trees. The growth of the plants and the quality of the fruits are very good,” he said.
Samirul added that expanding pineapple cultivation alongside mango orchards could create a new economic opportunity for the region. “The first harvest comes after 15 to 18 months. After that, the plants bear fruit every year without requiring replanting. Each plant produces four to five crowns, which can be sold as saplings or planted elsewhere,” he said.
He also said the agriculture department is providing overall support to Rayhan to encourage pineapple cultivation across the district.

item.title: Writ seeks HC probe into microplastics in 26 toothpaste brands in Bangladesh
item.description:
A writ petition has been filed with the High Court seeking an investigation into reports that 26 of 34 toothpaste products available in the Bangladeshi market contain potentially harmful microplastics.
Supreme Court lawyer Md Abdullah Al Mamun filed the petition on Monday.
The respondents include the secretaries of the Ministries of Health, Environment and Commerce, along with the Bangladesh Standards and Testing Institution (BSTI) and the Directorate of National Consumer Rights Protection (DNCRP).
The petition cites published media reports, which said microplastics were detected in 26 of the 34 toothpaste samples tested. The concentration of plastic particles ranged from 20 to 320 per 100 grams of toothpaste. The reports also said microplastics were found in four of the six toothpaste products formulated for children.
The findings were revealed in a recent study by the Environment and Social Development Organization (ESDO), which warned that the presence of microplastics in toothpaste poses potential risks to both human health and the environment.
According to the study, conducted between July 2025 and June 2026, researchers analysed 34 toothpaste samples representing 19 major brands manufactured in Bangladesh, India, Thailand and Vietnam.
Of the 25 locally manufactured samples, 22 were found to contain microplastics. Among the imported products, microplastics were detected in one of the five samples from India, one of the two samples from Thailand, and both samples imported from Vietnam.

“This initiative will provide investors with prompt approvals, straightforward utility connections, and essential administrative assistance. The government is committed to fulfilling every commitment made under the G2G agreement in a timely, transparent, and efficient manner,” he said.
The home minister said the industrial zone would create new opportunities for employment, skills development, and economic growth for local communities.
“It represents not merely an industrial zone but also a conduit for a long-term economic partnership between Bangladesh and China. This project will be pivotal in promoting sustainable industrialization and building a prosperous Bangladesh for future generations,” he added.
Salahuddin Ahmed also said the initiative reflects the enduring friendship, mutual trust, and strategic partnership between Bangladesh and China, while opening new opportunities in industrial production, global supply chains, technology transfer, and skilled human resource development.
Finance Minister Amir Khasru Mahmud Chowdhury, State Minister for Land Mir Mohammed Helal Uddin, Chinese Ambassador to Bangladesh Yao Wen, Bangladesh Economic Zones Authority Executive Chairman Chowdhury Ashiq Mahmud Bin Harun, China Economic and Industrial Zone Chairman Wang Benchian, and representatives from the public and private sectors of both countries attended the program.

item.title: DMP urges Dhaka residents to register with CIMS
item.description:
Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) has urged homeowners, tenants and mess (shared accommodation) members in the capital to register with the Citizen Information Management System (CIMS), saying the platform will strengthen technology-based policing and enhance public safety.
The digital information management system registers, stores and updates the basic information of homeowners, tenants and mess members living in Dhaka.
DMP launched the software-based CIMS at Ramna Police Station on September 1, 2016. The system was expanded to all police stations across the capital in 2017, while the CIMS mobile app was introduced in 2019 to simplify the registration process.
According to DMP, 3,673,238 households have been registered in the CIMS database, which contains information on more than 5 million citizens. Police said the registration process is ongoing and urged all residents of the capital to enroll.
Why register with CIMS
DMP said CIMS helps maintain accurate and up-to-date citizen information, making beat policing more effective. The database also supports crime prevention and investigation, assists in identifying missing persons, verifies the identities of suspected individuals and enables the rapid collection and use of information during emergencies.
How to register
CIMS registration forms are available at every police station and police outpost within the Dhaka metropolitan area. Citizens can collect a form, complete it and submit it to the relevant police station. DMP advises applicants to keep a photocopy of the completed form for their records before submitting it.
Each DMP police station is divided into multiple beats, with a designated beat officer assigned to each area. Residents may contact their respective beat officer for assistance whenever necessary.
If a resident changes address, they must register again with the police station responsible for their new address.
Benefits for homeowners and tenants
DMP said homeowners can use CIMS registration to verify the identities of prospective tenants, reducing the risk of criminals or fraudsters renting or taking shelter on their premises and helping them avoid unnecessary harassment.
For tenants, registration provides an opportunity to become acquainted with their local beat officer, receive police assistance more quickly when needed and benefit from identity verification.
Role in crime prevention
According to DMP, the CIMS database plays an important role in criminal investigations by helping identify absconding criminals, verify information on suspected individuals and support timely crime prevention efforts.
Police also said the system has strengthened beat policing and helped build greater trust between law enforcement agencies and the public.
DMP's appeal
The Dhaka Metropolitan Police has called on all homeowners, tenants and mess members in the capital to complete their CIMS registration to help build a safer and crime-free Dhaka.

item.title: PM joins Notun Kuri sports grand finale
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Monday joined the grand finale of the national-level Notun Kuri Sports 2025-26 at the Bangladesh Army Stadium in Dhaka.
The nationwide sporting event, organized under the supervision of the Ministry of Youth and Sports, was held with the theme: "Krira Hole Pesha, Paribar Pabe Bharosha (If sports becomes a profession, family will find security)."
The prime minister arrived at the venue at 4pm and was greeted by thousands of young spectators. He waved to the crowd, exchanged greetings with athletes on the field, and interacted with students in the galleries, encouraging them to pursue sports. More than 8,000 students attended the event.
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed and State Minister for Youth and Sports Md Aminul Haque accompanied the prime minister.
The Notun Kuri Sports program was launched on May 2 at Sylhet District Stadium with the aim of identifying sporting talent among boys and girls aged 12 to 14 and encouraging grassroots participation in sports.
According to the organizers, around 170,000 athletes from districts and upazilas across the country competed in the regional phase across 8 disciplines before advancing to the national-level competitions held in Dhaka.
This year's edition featured football, cricket, kabaddi, athletics, badminton, chess, swimming, and martial arts.
The closing ceremony included the boys' and girls' football finals and the boys' and girls' 100-meter sprint events.
In the boys' football final, Sylhet Region defeated Mymensingh Region 2-0.

Measles outbreak: Death toll reaches 825 as five die in 24 hours
item.description:
Five more children have died from measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours leading up to 8:00am on Monday, raising the overall death toll from the ongoing outbreak to 825.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) has classified all five of the latest casualties as suspected.
With the latest figures, the total number of suspected measles deaths has reached 730, while the number of confirmed deaths remained unchanged at 95, as no new confirmed measles deaths were reported in the last 24 hours.
Among the five new suspected fatalities, the highest concentration was recorded in Dhaka, with three deaths reported in both the Dhaka division and Dhaka district.
A total of 992 suspected measles cases were recorded in the 24 hours till Monday morning, taking the overall suspected case tally to 124,745.
During the same period, 113 new confirmed measles cases were reported, bringing the total number of confirmed infections to 15,555.
Since March 15, 2026, a total of 107,654 suspected measles patients have been hospitalized across the country, of whom 103,467 have recovered and been discharged from hospitals, according to the DGHS.

item.description:
The presidential election will be held on time and candidates for the post will be nominated according to the party’s decision, LGRD Minister Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir said on Monday.
He made the remarks while responding to journalists' questions after inaugurating the divisional office of the Bangladesh Rural Development Board (BRDB) in the Terminal area of Rangpur city.
Mirza Fakhrul said the BNP is a democratic political party.
“Through a long struggle, our party formed the government with a two-thirds majority in parliament with the love and votes of the people,” he said.
He said the BNP had fulfilled the responsibility of running the government not once, but five times. “Those who call BNP a fascist either lack knowledge or have developed such a mentality,” he added.
The minister also urged the Jamaat-e-Islami ameer to read his party’s constitution carefully and assess how democratic the party is.
Regarding local government elections, he said the Election Commission would decide on the issue of educational qualifications for candidates. “If not by the end of this year, the local government elections will be held early next year,” he said.
Mirza Fakhrul also said the government has waived interest on agricultural loans up to Tk10,000 to support agricultural development.
He added that the prime minister announced maximum allocation for agricultural development in the Rangpur region and that all necessary steps would be taken to make agriculture profitable.

item.title: Shapla Chattar case: Tribunal issues arrest warrants for Hasina, others
item.description:
The International Crimes Tribunal (ICT)-2 on Monday took cognizance of formal charges against 41 people, including fugitive former prime minister Sheikh Hasina and former army chief Gen Aziz Ahmed, in a case over alleged crimes against humanity linked to the May 5, 2013, crackdown on a Hefazat-e-Islam rally at Shapla Chattar in Motijheel.
The three-member tribunal, headed by Justice Nazrul Islam, also issued arrest warrants against Sheikh Hasina and the other fugitive accused after hearing the prosecution's application.
Among those for whom arrest warrants were issued are former prime minister Sheikh Hasina, former army chief Gen Aziz Ahmed and former inspector general of police (IGP) Benazir Ahmed.
Nine accused are currently in custody in the case. They are former minister Dr Dipu Moni, former state minister for home affairs Shamsul Hoque Tuku, retired Maj Gen Ziaul Ahsan, former IGP AKM Shahidul Haque, former deputy inspector general (DIG) Molla Nazrul Islam, Ekattorer Ghatak Dalal Nirmul Committee advisory council chairman Shahriar Kabir, former DIG Abdul Jalil Mondol, and journalists Farzana Rupa and Mozammel Babu.
Prosecutors Zahirul Amin, Moinul Karim and Marjina Raihan represented the prosecution during the submission of the formal charges.
The charge sheet also names former home minister Dr Mohiuddin Khan Alamgir, former information ministers Hasanul Haq Inu and Dr Hasan Mahmud, former food minister Dr Abdur Razzaque, Awami League leaders Sheikh Fazlul Karim Selim, Mahbubul Alam Hanif, AFM Bahauddin Nasim and Jahangir Kabir Nanak, former ministers Abdul Latif Siddiqui, Mofazzal Hossain Chowdhury Maya and Dr Dipu Moni, former Jubo League chairman Omar Faruk Chowdhury, former MP Salauddin Mahmud, Jana Jagaran Mancha spokesperson Dr Imran H Sarker, Ekattorer Ghatak Dalal Nirmul Committee president Shahriar Kabir, 71 TV Managing Director Mozammel Haque Babu, journalist Farzana Rupa, several former police chiefs and senior police officials, as well as former RAB and army officers.
On May 5, 2013, Hefazat-e-Islam Bangladesh held a rally at Shapla Chattar in Motijheel to press its 13-point demands. Following daylong tensions and clashes, police, the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) and Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) carried out a joint operation overnight to clear the area.
The International Crimes Tribunal later launched an investigation into allegations that many people were killed during the operation.

item.title: Amit: Gas supply to improve from next week, return to normalcy a week later
item.description:
State Minister for Power, Energy and Mineral Resources Aninda Islam Amit on Monday once again apologized to the public for the ongoing gas crisis, expressing hope that supply will begin to improve from next week, with full restoration expected about a week later.
Speaking to reporters at his office at the Secretariat, he said the government is making every possible effort to resolve the crisis, which has severely affected households, industries and transport services.
"We know homemakers are struggling to cook, industries have had to scale back production, and pressure on CNG stations has disrupted public transport. We sincerely apologies to the people for the hardship," the state minister said.
He said the disruption was not caused by any government agency but stemmed from a problem involving a private operator responsible for ensuring part of the country's gas supply.
"We are working jointly with them around the clock. We cannot provide an immediate solution due to certain limitations. However, our teams are working 24/7 with the company, and we hope the situation will start improving from next week, InshaAllah," Amit said.
Referring to the floating storage and regasification unit (FSRU) in Moheshkhali of Cox’s Bazar where the technical fault occurred, he said the facility normally supplies around 500 to 550 million cubic feet of gas per day.
According to information provided by the operator, the state minister said, the FSRU is expected to resume supplying around 280 to 300 million cubic feet of gas per day to the national grid from next week.
"If they can restore about 50% of the supply next week, the plan is to return to 100 percent capacity in the following week," he added.

item.title: Dismissed police personnel seek PM's intervention for reinstatement
item.description:
A group of dismissed police personnel on Monday urged the prime minister to intervene and ensure their reinstatement, claiming they were removed from service during the Awami League government's tenure due to political persecution rather than proven misconduct.
They made the demand during a human chain program held in front of the Jatiya Press Club in the capital.
Speaking at the program, representatives of the dismissed personnel said they were among 1,522 police officers and employees who had either been dismissed or forced into retirement without fair departmental inquiries.
They alleged that the previous government removed hundreds of honest and competent police personnel to serve political interests and suppress dissent.
According to the protesters, after the change in government, they appealed to the interim government for justice.
They claimed the home ministry later issued an order supporting their reinstatement on humanitarian grounds.
Following the ministry's decision, Police Headquarters formed a 10-member high-level committee, led by a Deputy Inspector General (DIG), to review the cases, they said. The committee reportedly examined the matter over six months before submitting four recommendations.
They also said Police Headquarters' media cell announced through the media on February 8, 2025, that the 1,522 dismissed police personnel would soon be reinstated, raising hopes among the affected members and their families.
However, they alleged that despite the Home Ministry's order, the committee's findings and the public announcement, the reinstatement process has yet to be implemented.
The protesters further claimed there had been inconsistencies in implementing the committee's recommendations. They alleged that although the committee recommended reinstating only those who had received two favorable verdicts from the Administrative Appellate Tribunal, some personnel with only one favorable verdict were later allowed to return to service.
Addressing the gathering, former Sub-Inspector Mamun Sirajul Haque urged the prime minister to ensure implementation of the home ministry's reinstatement order and the Police Headquarters committee's recommendations, expressing hope that the affected 1,522 families would be able to regain their livelihoods and return to serving the country.

item.title: Freedom fighter allowances increased from July 1
item.description:
The government has increased the monthly honorarium and other financial benefits for freedom fighters, families of martyred freedom fighters and war-wounded freedom fighters.
The revised rates, announced in a notification issued by the Budget Branch of the Ministry of Liberation War Affairs, will take effect from July 1, 2026.
Under the new rates, monthly honorariums, festival allowances, medical allowances and special grants for Victory Day and the Bangla New Year have been increased for various categories of freedom fighters and their families. Benefits for families of martyred freedom fighters have also been raised.
The ministry said the decision was taken under Section 3 of the Bangladesh Freedom Fighters Welfare Trust Act, 2018, and the relevant rules framed by the ministry, with the aim of strengthening the welfare, dignity and social security of freedom fighters.
Under the revised structure, recipients of the Bir Uttam title will receive a monthly honorarium of Tk30,000, along with Tk10,000 as a festival allowance, Tk5,000 on Victory Day and Tk2,000 for the Bangla New Year.
Recipients of the Bir Bikram and Bir Protik titles will receive a monthly honorarium of Tk25,000, as well as Tk10,000 in festival allowance, Tk5,000 for Victory Day and Tk2,000 for the Bangla New Year.
Families of martyred freedom fighters will receive a monthly honorarium of Tk23,000, a Tk2,000 medical allowance, a Tk5,000 food allowance, a festival allowance of Tk23,000 and Tk2,000 for the Bangla New Year.
The government has also revised monthly honorariums for war-wounded freedom fighters based on disability categories. Category A (96-100% disability) beneficiaries will receive Tk30,000 per month, Category B (61-95%) Tk28,000, Category C (20-60%) Tk23,000, and Category D (1-19%) Tk20,000.
The notification, signed by Deputy Secretary Dr Md Asaduzzaman, said the government is continuing to implement welfare programs to strengthen the financial security and social status of freedom fighters and their families. Source: BSS.
